blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The chapter structures the Freedom Movement in Karnataka into three distinct phases.
Early Resistance & Revolts represent the initial armed and local opposition to colonial rule.
The National Movement in Karnataka details the region's participation in the broader Indian struggle for independence.
Karnataka Unification outlines the political and social movement that led to the integration of Kannada-speaking regions.

cells: First armed resistance against British in Karnataka; refused to follow Doctrine of Lapse; fought Thackeray (British Collector); died in captivity 1829
Military commander of Rani Chennamma; continued guerrilla warfare; hanged by British at Nandagad in 1831; Karnataka's folk hero
Raja Venkatappa Nayaka of Surpura (Yadgir) revolted; part of 1857 Mutiny aftermath in Karnataka
Bhashkar Rao Bhat Nargundkar revolted; hanged in 1858
Chikka Viraraja of Kodagu — last king; deposed by British; exiled to Benares
Published 'Desher Katha'; inspired nationalism in Bengal-Karnataka link
Coined the name 'Karnataka'; wrote Karnataka Gatha Vaibhava; father of Karnataka unification movement
Congress leader; participated in Salt Satyagraha; later CM of Mysore; role in unification
Karnataka Congress leader; Non-Cooperation Movement; led KA unit
Civil Disobedience; Quit India Movement in Karnataka
Quit India Movement; underground activities in North Karnataka
Leader of Quit India Movement in Dharwad; fiery orator
Woman freedom fighter from Belagavi; participated in Civil Disobedience
While not a freedom fighter, pressured British for Mysore industries & education autonomy
Wrote Karnataka anthem 'Jaya Bharata Jananiya Tanujate'; inspired cultural nationalism

items: Focus on key leaders and armed uprisings during the Early Resistance & Revolts phase.
Understand the major events, non-cooperation initiatives, and Satyagrahas associated with the National Movement in Karnataka.
Memorize important conventions, conferences, and key personalities involved in the Karnataka Unification process.

cells: Kannada-speaking areas were split across Mysore State, Hyderabad, Bombay, Coorg, Madras and Central Provinces under British
Reorganised states on linguistic basis; all Kannada-speaking regions merged on November 1, 1956
Under Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs, State renamed from Mysore to Karnataka on November 1, 1973
Organisation that led the agitation for Kannada unification; Aluru Venkata Rao & others spearheaded it
